subject.title: Feature Request: Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool)

question: Should the model be permitted to request compaction of its own currently executing session through `session_status`, with no cross-session capability and recovery handled by the existing abort/compact/resume path?
rationale: This changes the trust boundary from user/operator-triggered or automatic maintenance to an explicit model-originated mutation of active session state; repository behavior cannot decide that policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve current-session only
options.body: Permit the narrow self-session action, fail closed outside an active run, and require current-main recovery and transcript-integrity proof.

options.title: Keep compaction external
options.body: Retain automatic, slash-command, CLI, and operator-RPC compaction without exposing a model-callable mutation.

options.title: Defer to continuation design
options.body: Pause the narrow PR until maintainers choose whether compaction should be part of a broader continuation framework.

recommendation.title: Approve current-session only
recommendation.body: Permit the narrow self-session action, fail closed outside an active run, and require current-main recovery and transcript-integrity proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and recently maintained the central `session_status` and session-resolution surfaces, making him the strongest history-backed owner for this boundary decision.
